items.text: A Wayne County homeowner reports a covered fire loss. The insurer never sends a written specification of what it needs for a satisfactory proof of loss. Under MCL 500.2006(3), how many days after receipt of the claim did that duty expire?

B. 30 days — MCL 500.2006(3) requires the insurer to specify in writing the materials for a satisfactory proof of loss not later than 30 days after receipt of a claim, unless settled within the 30 days.

Under MCL 500.2006(3), if a proof of loss covers only part of a claim, the supported amount is considered timely paid if paid within how many days after the insurer's receipt of that partial proof of loss?
C. 60 days — Subsection (3) considers a partial claim timely paid if paid within 60 days after receipt of proof of loss for that portion; any later-supplied remainder gets its own 60-day clock.

A mortgagee is named on a fire policy and the insured fails to render a proof of loss. Under MCL 500.2833(1)(j), how many days after the insurer's notice does the mortgagee have to render its own proof of loss?
C. 60 days — MCL 500.2833(1)(j) gives the mortgagee 60 days after notice from the insurer to render proof of loss, when the insured has failed to do so herself.
Under MCL 500.2833(1)(l), what does the statute itself set as the deadline for the insured to give notice when a loss occurs?

D. No fixed day count; the policy sets it — Section 2833(1)(l) only requires the policy to contain 'the notification requirements when a loss occurs.' The statute sets no day count for the insured; the policy's Conditions section does.
A proof of the amount of loss is received by the insurer on February 1. Under MCL 500.2833(1)(p) and MCL 500.2836(2), by what date must the loss be paid?
B. March 3 — Both sections require payment within 30 days after receipt of proof of amount of loss; 30 days after February 1 is March 3.
Using the same February 1 proof-of-loss date, if the claim remains unpaid, on what date does MCL 500.2006(4)'s 12% simple interest begin accruing?

C. April 2 — Interest under MCL 500.2006(4) accrues from a date 60 days after satisfactory proof of loss was received, which is April 2, sixty days after February 1. This is a separate clock from the 30-day payment deadline.
Under MCL 500.2006(4), the 'reasonably in dispute' defense to owing 12% interest applies to which type of claimant?

B. A third-party tort claimant — Subsection (4) writes the reasonable-dispute defense only into the third-party tort claimant sentence. First-party insureds get the 12% regardless of dispute, per Griswold Properties LLC v Lexington Ins Co, 276 Mich App 551 (2007), and Nickola v MIC General Ins Co, 500 Mich 115 (2017).

A homeowner and her insurer disagree only about the amount of a covered loss. She serves a written appraisal demand. Under MCL 500.2833(1)(m), how many days does the insurer have to name its appraiser?
C. 20 days — MCL 500.2833(1)(m) gives each party 20 days after receipt of the written demand to name a competent, independent appraiser.
The two appraisers in an MCL 500.2833(1)(m) appraisal cannot agree on an umpire. How many days must pass before either side may ask the circuit court to appoint one?
B. 15 days — The statute allows either side to petition the circuit court for the county of loss if the two appraisers are unable to agree upon an umpire within 15 days.
Under MCL 500.2833(1)(m), an appraisal award binds the parties on which issue?

B. Amount of loss only — Appraisal sets the amount of the loss and actual cash value only; it never decides coverage. Auto-Owners Ins Co v Kwaiser, 190 Mich App 482 (1991): 'the issue of coverage is for the court, not the appraisers.'

A Michigan carrier nonrenews a homeowners policy in 2026, citing 3 paid claims in the last 3 years totaling $4,200, none of them weather-related. Under MCL 500.2117(2)(e)(i), as the dollar minimums stand today, what is the exclusive-of-weather threshold the carrier must clear?

A. $5,000 — MCL 500.2117(2)(e)(i) prints $3,000, but MCL 500.2117(5) indexes the minimums to the consumer price index every sixth year, certified by DIFS bulletin. Bulletin 2024-02-INS raised the exclusive-of-weather minimum to $5,000 effective January 1, 2024, so $4,200 does not clear it. The $4,000 option is the pre-2024 certified figure and $6,600 is the including-weather figure.

A carrier wants to nonrenew a homeowner's policy for reasons other than nonpayment of premium. Under MCL 500.2123(1), confirmed by DIFS Bulletin 2025-12-INS, how many days' notice must it give before the termination is effective?

C. 30 days — MCL 500.2123(1) requires at least 30 days' written notice before a termination is effective. DIFS Bulletin 2025-12-INS confirms this is the controlling day count for home-insurance cancellation and nonrenewal.
A policy was issued 40 days ago. Under MCL 500.2123(2), what is the shortest notice period the insurer could use to make a termination effective?
B. 20 days — Because the policy is within its first 55 days, MCL 500.2123(2) allows a notice mailed or delivered in that window to be effective as little as 20 days after mailing or delivery.
Under MCL 500.2117, which of the following is a listed permitted ground for refusing, limiting, or nonrenewing home insurance?

C. A changed adjacent physical hazard since the original date of issuance — MCL 500.2117(2)(h) allows underwriting rules based on the existence of an adjacent physical hazard where the hazard has changed since the original date of issuance; the other options are not on the statute's closed list and several are independently unlawful discrimination grounds.
According to DIFS Bulletin 2025-12-INS, are mere cosmetic roof issues such as discoloration or streaking, seen in aerial imagery, valid grounds for cancellation or nonrenewal?
C. No, they are not valid grounds — The bulletin states plainly that mere cosmetic roof issues, such as discoloration or streaking, are not valid grounds for policy cancellation or nonrenewal.

A homeowner's claim is unresolved after 8 months. She wants to know whether the 1-year suit limitation in MCL 500.2833(1)(q) has already expired. She gave notice of loss 2 days after the loss and the insurer has never formally denied the claim. What is the state of the suit clock?

B. It is tolled and has not been running since notice was given, aside from the initial 2 days — MCL 500.2833(1)(q) tolls the suit-limitation period from the time the insured notifies the insurer of the loss until the insurer formally denies liability. With no formal denial, only the days before notice count against the year.
According to the DIFS complaint page (michigan.gov/difs/consumers/complaint), what day count does DIFS state for its own response time or for how fast a carrier must respond to a complaint?

D. No day count is stated — The DIFS page fetched for this domain states no fixed timeline for DIFS's own response or for the carrier's response; any claim of a specific forced response window is unsupported.
Under MCL 500.2026(2), what is an insurer required to maintain regarding complaints from its insureds?

B. A complete record since the last examination, including total complaints, classification, nature, disposition, and processing time — MCL 500.2026(2) makes it an unfair practice to fail to maintain a complete record of all insured complaints since the last examination, showing the total number, classification by line, nature, disposition, and processing time.
For a Fannie Mae-owned mortgage loan that is current at the time of an insured loss, Servicing Guide B-5-01 authorizes an initial disbursement up to the greater of which set of figures?

C. $40,000 or 33% of proceeds — B-5-01 authorizes an initial disbursement up to the greater of $40,000; 33% of the insurance loss proceeds; or the amount by which release funds exceed the loan's UPB, accrued interest, and advances.
Under DIFS Bulletin 2026-16-INS, the fire insurance maximum escrow withholding effective July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027 under MCL 500.2227 is what amount?

D. $25,090 — Bulletin 2026-16-INS sets the MCL 500.2227 maximum withholding at $25,090 for the period July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027, up from $24,096 the prior year. The $16,383 figure belongs to the separate MCL 500.2845 calendar-year escrow, a different section entirely.
